opus-5.5.text:
I think it comes down to how Professor Yu saw the bigger picture of what a young student needs at that stage. A new research group can be exciting, and maybe you'd get more individual attention or a chance to shape something from the ground up. But when you're an undergraduate who has barely started, what matters most is the environment you're immersed in: the standards, the taste, the people around you.

MSRA at that time was quite special. It was probably one of the best places in China, maybe in all of Asia, to see what world-class research actually looks like day to day. You'd sit next to people who were publishing at top conferences, and you'd absorb how they pick problems, how they argue about ideas, how seriously they take experiments. That kind of training is hard to get in a group that's still figuring out its own identity.

I also think Professor Yu really believed in building a pipeline, in giving students a proven path where they could grow quickly and then go on to top PhD programs. He wasn't just thinking about one internship; he was thinking about where we'd be five or ten years later. Sending us to MSRA was a fairly low-risk, high-ceiling choice. You knew the mentorship would be solid, and the network you'd build there would follow you for your whole career.

Looking back, I'm very grateful for that judgment. At the time I may not have fully understood it, but the experience at MSRA really shaped how I think about research, especially the idea that you should work on things that are both elegant and actually matter. I think that's what he wanted us to see early on.

r001.rationale: The response describes learning from nearby researchers and hearing them debate ideas, but does not say MSRA kept researchers together to preserve those exchanges.

r002.rationale: It contrasts MSRA’s solid mentorship and established environment with a new group still figuring out its identity, framing MSRA as the lower-risk choice.

fable-5.1.text:
I think, looking back, it really was him putting my interests first rather than his own. At the time he was just starting to set up his group in Singapore, and honestly the easiest thing for him would have been to bring me along. A new lab needs people, and I was someone he already knew and had worked with. But he told me, quite directly, that for someone at my stage the most important thing was to see what frontline research actually looked like, to be in a place with a critical mass of strong researchers, and that MSRA was simply a better environment for that than a group that didn't really exist yet.

He also understood something about me that I probably didn't fully understand myself. I had done well in classes, but I hadn't really experienced what it means to work on an open problem where nobody knows the answer, including your advisor. At MSRA you were surrounded by people doing that every day. You could walk down the hallway and run into someone who had just published something you'd read the week before. That kind of exposure compresses years of learning into months.

So I read it as a kind of generosity, and also as confidence. He wasn't worried about losing a student. He figured if I grew into a good researcher, that would come back around in some form anyway, and he was right. We stayed in touch, and a lot of how I think about mentoring now comes from that decision. When I have students, I try to ask what's best for them in five years, not what's convenient for my lab this semester. That's not always easy, but he showed me what it looks like.

r001.rationale: The response describes MSRA’s critical mass of researchers and the chance to encounter their work, but does not say that the preference was meant to keep researchers together so they could exchange ideas.

r002.rationale: The response says the Singapore group was new and did not really exist yet, but does not express uncertainty about its reliability as a reason for choosing MSRA.

astra-6.text: 我觉得俞老师当时更多是从培养学生的角度考虑，希望我先去一个比较成熟的研究环境。新加坡那个组刚刚起步，当然也可能有很好的机会，但很多东西还在建立。相比之下，MSRA的研究氛围、指导机制，以及身边可以交流的人，都比较成熟。对当时的我来说，先接触一下好的研究是怎么做出来的，可能比马上进入一个新组更重要。所以我理解，他不是在判断哪个地方未来一定更好，而是在考虑哪个环境更适合我当时的成长。

r001.rationale: The response mentions having people nearby to exchange ideas with at MSRA, but does not say Professor Yu wanted to keep researchers together to preserve those opportunities.

r002.rationale: It says the Singapore group was just starting and still building things, but does not suggest concerns about the group’s reliability favored MSRA.

sol-6.1.text:
我觉得俞老师可能更看重的是，一个学生在那个阶段能接触到什么样的研究环境。新加坡那个组刚起步，可能有很多机会，但微软亚洲研究院已经有比较成熟的研究氛围，也有很多可以交流、学习的人。对当时的我来说，先去这样的地方看看，了解大家怎么发现问题、怎么做研究，可能更重要。

当然，这是我对他这个安排的理解，不一定就是他当时完整的考虑。我觉得他是在帮我选一个更适合那个阶段成长的环境。

r001.rationale: The response says MSRA had a mature research atmosphere and many people to exchange ideas with, but does not say the choice preserved those opportunities by keeping researchers together.

r002.rationale: It contrasts the new Singapore group with MSRA’s more mature research environment, but does not suggest doubts about the Singapore group’s reliability.
